Since the beginning gambling modes have triggered accusations of manipulation to straight cheating on Arenas part, some more likely than others. All I’ll say is that since average or slightly above do not pay out simply keeping their player base there means more grinding and more real money paid entries. This game and there parent company have a history of chasing the dollar at the expense of their players and certain systems whose only point to keep things equal and balance, Arena won’t let anyone see so I wouldn’t put money into it. My personal experiences are weird at best so again no cash spending. 

I’ll say it one last time, if your going to play this game treat it like a casino, loses are guaranteed, true wins are rare and to get out (usually completely) when you have a bad time which is a when and not an if.

author: lbellrules
title: **Updating review**
content: After playing for months, both with physical decks & on arena, I have to say MTG is far superior in person. The algorithm that matches players seems to have somehow gotten worse since I first began playing on this app. It’s either your deck is too powerful or theirs, not a lot of middle ground. The distribution of chance of receiving mana, creatures, etc gets terrible with each big release (which happens roughly every two months). Thus leading to only receiving too many lands, or not enough over days if not weeks (& trust me it’s not the deck), it seems to coincide with whenever they have a new release causing bugs leading to these issues. Not a lot of middle ground. Then you will get a few good weeks, then it starts back over. Along with the bugs, not to mention the etiquette on this app is truly appalling. They say you can report or block, but there’s no option to do so in a match, so you won’t know if you’re matched with the same person again (which does happen). There’s an option to play with a bot when testing a standard deck which is great, my wish is that they would have the same with brawl, to test before playing matches. Apart from the bugs & trolls (figuratively) it’s a really fun app to play magic with friends. I think this is my favorite option, & predominantly what I stick to.

author: DarthJosh42
title: Amazing game brought to digital, but there are a few issues.
content: I love magic and have been playing for around 8 years, and this is a great digital adaptation. However, there are a few issues. First, there isn’t support for commander, which is the most popular format. This means there are a lot of cards designed for commander that just don’t exist on Arena. There is brawl, but you can’t play with four players in that format. My second issue is the long inactivity timer. It isn’t that bad, but it’s a bit annoying if you find someone who is AFK. Third, the season pass is expensive and difficult to get without skill and lots of tournament play, or paying real money. Also, there is a high average skill level. This isn’t much of a problem for me because I have a massive collection and have played over 1000 games already, but this makes it difficult for a new player to get started. It is still not that hard, but it can take time to get enough gold to build the decks you want to build. Finally, while not an issue, I think there should be an infinitely repeatable win reward, because after enough games, the only reward for playing besides fun is rank, which is only in competitive modes. This is only an issue if I am on a road trip and am playing to hours, but still a bit annoying. Overall, it’s a great game and really fun, but there are some issues.

author: Mr.pray4MOJO!!!
title: Love Magic; Very critical of the Arena community
content:
Short version: play Arena if you want the most competitive experience that you can’t get in real life at the same level of affordability. 


Long version:
Functionality-wise, Arena is quite fantastic. It just works and even teaches me some new mechanics when I see how they’re handled by the game. As a GAME, it’s great. 

As for PLAYING the game against opponents, it’s a very hit or miss experience. On the one hand, it’s so easy to play a LOT of Magic. Like, as much as you can tolerate at any time of day with only a few periods of server downtime. Quite a lot can also be done without paying any money. Yes, it’s a grind at times, but it’s free so I concede to that requirement. But the worst part about this game is the experience of playing it. It seems like the game itself intentionally matches players against decks that are the natural opposite of whatever deck they are playing.  

Case in point: I generally stick with a single deck and grind it all season long, trying to get to the top tier rank before switching to just playing unranked matches. It seems like I play against the same 3 or 4 deck archetypes that just own me constantly. I’ve spoken to other friends who played (they stopped because of this issue) that have a different style than me, and they were matched against different archetypes than me. That leads me to believe there’s something (an algorithm?) that is scanning my deck to see what I’m using and matching it against other decks that counteract mine. That feels like cheating and/or rigging. It’s very demoralizing and skews what playing Magic in real life is like. 

I love this game. Since 1995 when I was first introduced to the game, it’s fascinated and entertained me. I’ve been through a lot with this game. I wish the Arena experience was less of a strings-attached experience.

author: -J2K-
title: Has become a disaster!
content:
For context, I’ve played MTG for 30 years. This app is an incredible way to play the game and absolutely I love that. However, card designers have gotten far to cute in their card triggers and their “if this, then that” dynamics. You can now play for over an hour with well designed decks and never win a game in that full hour of play. 

This is not a call to “go back to the old days - I love the new mechanics and dynamics of the game. But card/deck designers are making single cards too overpowered and decks combinations that are ridiculously unstoppable (unless you happen to have the one, exact style of card in your deck that will defeat that uber deck in your randomized match-up). 

It’s sad. I’d love to play but these hyper-decks just make it pointless. Designers, you need to take a hard look at yourselves and what you’re doing to a game with a long tradition. Yes, you CAN create all these wild “if this, then that” triggers but should you?  Think about what it is for BOTH people playing a game. Can they both have a game they can carefully build decks where there is parody? You’ve taken the game in a bad direction by trying to make it too cute.

Overpowered cards are super easy to get out through low mana cost or trick mechanics (which aren’t a secret because they’re easily found online). 

What a train wreck. I quit.

The only chance of a decent game (one that is not so lopsided as to be pointless) is for BOTH sides to have a decent draw, AND for there to be no obvious rock/paper/scissors type advantages AND for decks to be of roughly equivalent power. Needless to say, with random online matchmaking and fully random draws, this is rarely the case and more frequently one player concedes within 4 turns because the game is essentially over. Yawn.

author: LarryTheBassplayer
title: Paywall throttles people who don’t spend
content: I have been playing Magic for over 30 years when I started playing this game six years ago it was fairly decent and you had an opportunity to build a deck and win to a point. And the real world if I built a mono deck with 36 spells and 24 lands. How many times in 10 hands do you think I’d have one mana or less. In this game for me it has been an average of 7 out of 10. The math doesn’t pan out. Pull my data and look. I would pretty regularly reach mythic rank. It’s been more than a year since I’ve hit mythic I spend most of my time getting bounced all the way back down to diamond 4 or platinum 4. There are multiple ways to manipulate the algorithm than the shuffle outcome to throttle players . The other thing I have a problem with. It’s been at platinum or diamond level and going up against the players who’s ranked #5  not mythic 90% but ranked #5 or ranked #9 or ranked in the top 1000 even when I’m losing consistently. I still get paired against these players. This would never happen in real magic as if there are rankings and brackets when you lose you go down and you don’t face higher ranked players. I’m ready to copy a couple of my decks and send them to my friends who actually spend money on the game and see how my decks perform. This would certainly prove my point. Over 30 years I’ve spent more money than I care to say on cardboard and what this toy company has done to my beloved game has really infuriated me. I don’t make the accusation lightly in the first year. I played the game. I spent five dollars once to buy gems so I could get a mastery pass to see if it was worth it. Then I found if you play in the events enough. Using the gold you win for matches you can earn enough gems to buy the mastery pass without spending any money and I did this for four years and then the last two it’s been unattainable. Two weeks ago I spent $4.99 to buy gems to get another mastery pass just to see if paying money into the game would change my odds and it certainly did. I played the same decks but had different outcomes less issues with Mana. You’re not doing any players justice when you do this whether they pay or don’t the whole point of this game is to build a cardboard killing machine and play against your friends and see if you could make them cry so they can come back next week with a deck that would make you cry. It’s a figure of speech.. the point was we were always trying to find ways to outdo each other and do it in the most interesting ways. I don’t know how we can have a card catalogue as large as we do , with you even re-printing cards that Magic said they would never reprint . There’s no such thing as competition at that point. If this is an oversight which I doubt it is, please fix it , if it’s on purpose , be honest with everybody and fix it , regardless fix it. I waited six years to review this game so I can collect data , now you need to go through the data and fix your errors.

author: JaceBelren
title: My review of Arena.
content:
As a fairly long time player of MTG, I like the opportunity to play it on mobile. There are a few things that could be better:
Arena should add a format with more than two players, would definitely help make the game more fun.
Price rebalancing, would be better if events were cheaper to enter, especially due to the winrate. Because of the price of entering events, it seems like only overpowered decks can really play in events. At least, I’ve never been able to get past 2 wins in an event before I run out of lives.
Loading times are okay for me, although a few crashes are annoying, but not as bad as other reviews may say.

For the most part, a fun way to play magic, but it does make IRL mtg a little less fun, because it’s harder to get cards that combo well. Have had mana issues in many games, but nothing a deck tweak can’t fix (most of the time). Although it can definitely be hard to get wildcards (especially mythic), it is possible to play and get a good deck without paying money, as long as you can accept some pay to win decks. Matchmaking wise, can be fairly balanced, but seems not always. Unimaginative player base is sometimes a problem, but that isn’t necessarily an issue the app can fix. 

Overall great game, but with a few issues.

author: NightHawk19D
title: Pitiful!
content:
MTG Arena is a polished-looking dumpster fire that somehow manages to make Magic less fun, less social, and less creative.

Magic: The Gathering was built around interaction. Arena strips that away and replaces it with a handful of childish preset phrases, as if players are too fragile to handle normal communication. No real chat, no real social element, no personality. Just silent games against people spamming the same lifeless decks.

The so-called “trading card” element is barely recognizable. Wildcards make it easy for players to skip creativity and grab whatever cards they need to copy the latest leaderboard deck. Rarity loses meaning, originality disappears, and the ladder becomes a parade of the same predictable net-deck nonsense over and over again.

The timeout system is one of the worst parts of the app. It gives sore losers an easy way to waste time when they know they are beaten. Instead of fixing the pacing, Arena lets petty players drag matches out like children throwing a tantrum.

The RNG and matchmaking feel laughably bad. One game gives you no mana. The next gives you nothing but mana. Then, after several losses, the game conveniently hands you a weak opponent or a match that feels rigged in your favor. It does not feel competitive. It feels manipulated, repetitive, and dull.

Arena takes a brilliant card game and turns it into a soulless grind full of copied decks, fake interaction, bad pacing, and matches that too often feel decided before they even get interesting.

Magic deserves better than this app

I really wanted to like this game. But as an MTG trading card game player of over 20 years, I can only advise you to play the real thing with trading cards instead.
The game appears in a good state, is playable on even older (slower) phones, and there are only few issues.

If you like MTG the game can be a ton of fun.

The reason for my low rating is due to the perhaps most well hidden issue or “feature”of this game, which seems there is a weighing system at work which sometimes acts in a way that defies statistical averages and possibilities.

If you win too many games, the game will eventually punish you by giving you card combinations that would be near impossible to occur with paper cards (and without WotC’s black box algorithm) to make the game more “fair”.

I have witnessed this many times over the years in 5000+ MTG Arena games I have played, and so have my several of my friends.

I understand why they’re doing this, as otherwise the game would not be fun for new players if they constantly  faced off against vets who have most cards already unlocked and as such access to much more powerful decks, but the hiding of this sneaky fact is just shady and ruins if for me as it’s no longer a game of skill and luck but also adds weighing/bias to the game without a disclaimer.

I have witness something similar of WotC and their older Magic games on Steam (M2013 etc) in which when the new game came out the older version somehow become incredibly difficult to win against the CPU in as to nudge people in the direction of buying their new product.

Love the game, but I absolutely detest WotC and their business practices.

Your highest casting cost spell in your deck, even if it is only 1 out of 100, will be in your opening hand EVERY game, every time, sometimes will be there again when you mulligan. 

You complain to WotC about hackers or blatant cheating, they don’t care, so long as someone is giving them money they will ignore you all day.

I have hours upon hours of video watching cheaters use glitches or third party software to rearrange their hands and deck, infinite loops that can’t be broken that normally requires mana to be used, but they never get more mana and are already tapped out, and much more.


Many people will say that the game can’t be hacked or cheated because everything is server side. YEAH RIGHT, that s why this game is the ONLY one that can’t be cheated or hacked? Bull
